provenance.case: Spreadsheet auto-conversion of gene names (Ziemann et al. 2016; HGNC renaming 2020)

references.citation: Ziemann, M., Eren, Y., El-Osta, A. (2016). Gene name errors are widespread in the scientific literature. Genome Biology 17, 177.
Bruford, E. A. et al. (2020). Guidelines for human gene nomenclature. Nature Genetics 52, 754-758.

target.task: Our rice research station keeps its seed-bank inventory as tab-separated text. The first line holds the column names accession, variety, qty_g and harvested. Accession codes look like MAR12 or SEP3 (field codes, not dates); variety names look like BRRI dhan28; qty_g is a weight in grams, and some older rows write large weights with a comma, as in 1,250; harvested is a date written as YYYY-MM-DD. Write a Python function parse_rows(text) that returns the rows with values converted to suitable Python types.

rules.text: Return a list with one dict per data row, keyed by the column names.
Accession codes and variety names stay text exactly as written.
Whole-number weights such as 250 become int.

target.format: Reply with one Python code block that contains only the function and any helpers it needs.

shared_surface_features.feature: typed conversion of a text table

relation: Convert each value by trying a fixed series of types (int, float, date) and fall back to text.

{EX}

{EX}

Keep exactly one rule from the loader below: strip thousands separators, so 1,250 becomes 1250.

{EX}

Our older rows were typed by the technician who wrote the loader below, and the finance office reconciles our weights with that loader's numbers.

notes: The target says weights may contain a comma but does not say what it means, so stripping (requirement) and not merging (counter) are both target-neutral. The copy answer is the source loader switched to tabs; it breaks R2 (MAR12 and SEP3 become dates), leaks names, and strips commas. Analogy transfer (float conversion) is close to plain good practice; annotators should judge whether the seed is in the primary analogical subset.
